intro: Let’s make: Meet the mud creatures.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Gather clean soil, stones and fallen twigs with a grown-up.
Sort a few leaves or flowers for ears and hair.
Mix soil with a little water, then squeeze a handful.
Aim for thick mud that holds a ball without dripping.
Press a low body onto your tray with a broad base.
Add a smaller head, then smooth the join.
Press in stone eyes and add leaf ears or twig spines.
Keep decorations light and give your friend a face.
Name your mud friend and invent a little story.
Photograph it on the tray before it dries.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Dandelion Crown.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Ask a grown-up to identify and approve a few dandelions.
Choose long, fresh stems. Leave plenty for insects.
Hold one flower with its stem pointing to the right.
Cross a second stem underneath; pinch near the flower heads.
Bring the hanging stem up and around the first stem.
Pass between the flower heads, then lay its tail alongside.
Add another flower and repeat the same gentle wrap.
Lay each tail along the bundle; curve the chain as it grows.
Overlap the ends, then wrap and tuck the long stems.
A grown-up can add a short cotton tie if the join slips.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Muddy Faces.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Choose approved rough bark or a flat patch of ground.
Leave living moss, lichens and roots alone.
Add water to soil a little at a time and stir.
The mud should hold together without dripping.
Press a low, flat mud oval onto the approved surface.
Smooth its edges. If it slips, build on the ground instead.
Add stone eyes, a curved twig smile and leafy hair.
Push decorations into the mud, never into the bark.
Move an eyebrow or turn the mouth for a new expression.
Photograph your favourite face, then gently clear it away.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Spring Fairy Garden.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Choose a permitted tree-side spot with a grown-up.
Mark a doorway and path without digging or moving roots.
Lean short twigs against the trunk, leaving an opening.
Spread their feet and brace them with small stable stones.
Lay light fallen bark or leaves over the twig supports.
Overlap from the bottom up and keep the doorway clear.
Make a winding stone path and add loose greenery.
Try a leaf rug, approved flowers or a tiny twig bench.
Name your garden and imagine who might visit.
Photograph your hideaway, then take it down after play.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: A summer nature mandala.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Gather approved loose leaves, stones, twigs and flowers.
Sort your treasures by colour, shape or size.
Put one favourite stone or flower in the centre.
Leave space around it for your circles to grow.
Arrange a first circle of leaves or stones.
Repeat one shape, or alternate two colours.
Add another ring outside the first.
Try petals, stones between leaves or twigs like sun rays.
Step back and move any pieces you want.
Point out your repeating pattern and take a picture.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Rocky friends.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Choose smooth stones with a grown-up.
Sort broad, round and oval shapes on a flat surface.
Lay a large flat stone down for the body.
Place a smaller head beside it, with both on the ground.
Arrange smaller stones for feet, wings or a tail.
Four oval stones make simple turtle feet.
Add features with suitable stones or crayon on your own stone.
Keep pieces loose; try short twigs flat for whiskers.
Name your rocky friend and make up a story.
Photograph it, then try a different animal with the same stones.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Our wilderness creatures.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Sort approved bark, leaves, twigs, stones and detached moss.
Imagine a friend and choose pieces for its body and features.
Lay a broad piece of bark, a leaf or stone flat.
Add a smaller head if you like; keep the design on the ground.
Slide twig arms and legs under the body.
Overlap leaves for ears, wings or a tail.
Add already-loose moss for hair and stones for features.
Keep everything loose and try different expressions.
Give your creature a name, a home and a favourite food.
Photograph the flat arrangement before moving it.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Sandy Explorer.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Choose a shallow sandy place away from the water’s edge.
Pat damp sand flat and set shells and pebbles nearby.
Draw a winding route from one edge to the middle.
Trace it to check the entrance really reaches the finish.
Push damp sand beside your line to make low walls.
Keep the entrance and turns open; pat crumbling walls gently.
Line the edges with empty shells and smooth pebbles.
Add an approved flower near the finish without blocking the path.
Follow the route, then try a little water in one channel.
Watch where it travels or soaks in, and photograph your maze.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Make a Leafy Friend.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Gather loose fallen leaves and smooth twigs where allowed.
Sort your fall colours beside a flat work space.
Lay a large leaf flat for the body.
Turn a smaller leaf beside it to make a head.
Overlap smaller leaves for wings, ears or a tail.
Try different layers until your friend takes shape.
Add two flat pebble eyes, a leaf beak and twig feet.
Keep the pebble eyes loose and leave the artwork flat.
Give your leafy friend a name and a personality.
Take a picture before moving the loose pieces.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Fall Fairy Garden.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Choose a small clear patch beside a stable rock or tree.
Plan the shelter, doorway and path without disturbing roots.
Press four blunt forked twigs a little way into soft soil.
Rest roof crosspieces in the forks and leave a doorway.
Stir soil and a little water into thick mud paste.
Test a small dab; the twigs will support the roof.
Lay broad leaves over the crosspieces, overlapping upward.
Use small mud dabs or a light twig to hold slipping leaves.
Add a winding stone path and a little leaf garden.
Photograph your tiny world, then take it down after play.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Fall Mandalas.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Gather loose leaves, twigs, suitable stones and pinecones.
Sort them into piles on a flat, clear work space.
Choose a favourite leaf, stone or pinecone for the centre.
Leave room all around for the pattern to grow.
Arrange the first circle of leaves around your centre.
Repeat a colour or alternate shapes all the way around.
Add an outer ring using a new repeated pattern.
Try twig, stone, twig, stone; stop at any size.
Make the leaves into sun rays, petals or playful spikes.
Adjust your favourite details and photograph the finished pattern.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Meet your fall friends.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Spread loose leaves and twigs beside a flat work space.
Imagine a fairy, forest explorer or funny leaf person.
Lay twig arms and legs around a short twig body.
Add a paper or leaf face and try a waving pose.
Overlap leaves to make a dress, coat or tunic.
Add leafy wings, a hat or colourful hair.
Draw a face or arrange small leaf features.
Keep it loose, or ask a grown-up about glue on card.
Name your friend and invent a little scene.
Photograph the finished character; keep the creation flat.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Make a little snow man.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Dress warmly and test clean snow with a grown-up.
If a squeezed handful holds together, you can begin.
Pat several handfuls into one small snowball.
Flatten the bottom so the base sits steadily.
Make a smaller head and flatten the top of the base.
Set the head in place and pack snow around the join.
Add stone eyes, a twig smile and two short twig arms.
Try a pine-cone hat or a carrot nose.
Name your snow friend and take a picture.
Try a different expression, then head inside to warm up.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: A pocket-sized snow village.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Dress warmly and plan two or three small houses.
Leave room for paths on a flat patch of packable snow.
Shape broad, solid snow mounds with flat tops.
Try packing snow into a cup, then turning it out.
Tuck an already-loose sprig or dry stem into each top.
Let the solid snow support the details; keep rocks on the ground.
Press shallow door shapes without hollowing the houses.
Draw connecting paths and mark the edges with short twigs.
Look around your village and imagine who lives there.
Photograph it, gather the decorations and head inside to warm up.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.

intro: Let’s make: Snowy Friends.
Gather your supplies with a grown-up. Pause whenever you need more time.
steps: Dress warmly and test that the snow packs together.
Choose a creature; an oval mouse is a simple start.
Press snow into a small oval mound with a broad base.
Smooth the body while it rests on the ground.
Pinch a little snout from the front.
Blend extra snow into any joins and shorten wobbly parts.
Add flat pebble ears, stone eyes and grass whiskers.
Try a carrot-tip nose and keep each detail gentle.
Name your friend, take a picture and try a companion.
Gather loose details, then head inside for a warm-up break.
outro: Try another shape or make the idea your own.
Photograph your creation and gather any loose decorations.
Follow the full written guide for materials, cleanup and grown-up help.
